experiment_queue.formula: priority = decision_information * (0.6 + 0.4 * feasibility) * (0.7 + 0.3 * reuse) / cost_index, refused when the closed premise risk is at or above one half or the oracle headroom is zero

candidates.title: self model calibration against the temporal program's own history
candidates.question: does updating a self model beat a fixed prior of the same form on real paired outcomes

justification.bed: the temporal program's sealed shard receipts carry predicted and actual wall seconds, failures and quarantines. The bed exists already and this program did not design it
justification.oracle_headroom: a fixed prior is measurably miscalibrated on any stream with drift, and the temporal run has drifted across three resource classes
justification.cost: reading sealed receipts, no principal compute

candidates.title: perspective diversity against the best single perspective
candidates.question: does a heterogeneous perspective set beat the strongest single one at matched compute

justification.oracle_headroom: unmeasured. The perspectives are implemented but no bed has scored them
justification.instrumentation_risk: the six implemented perspectives read different regions, so a bed has to supply information for all of them or the comparison is unfair

candidates.title: owned continuity against matched budget transcript replay
candidates.question: does owned state restore more than a transcript replay of the same size

justification.instrumentation_risk: high. On a synthetic session the transcript length is a design choice, so the margin is set by how much filler the generator adds. This is the SX1 objection in a different costume and needs a session nobody wrote for the purpose
justification.oracle_headroom: unbounded replay recovers three of five probes on the demo, so a real ceiling exists, but not one this program has measured on an undesigned session

candidates.title: typed workspace on a bed with a larger reliability spread
candidates.question: does a fitted write restriction transfer to unseen source groups

justification.oracle_headroom: measured at 0.036 and 0.038 on the only two valid beds, both below the SESOI
justification.closed_premise: not closed, but no instrument currently reaches it

candidates.title: learned plasticity policy against the strongest simple rule
candidates.question: does a learned plasticity policy beat a simple triggered rule
candidates.refusal_reason: risk of repeating a closed premise is at or above one half

justification.closed_premise: the fast state program measured no stable headroom and sealed the null. Rerunning it without new headroom repeats a closed premise

experiment_queue.program_lesson: a Substrate hypothesis whose mechanism is a design choice needs a bed the program did not design. On a synthetic bed the oracle ceiling is whatever the generator was told to make it, and the experiment measures the generator. That axis is scored as instrumentation_risk

selection_rule: expected decision information, scientific headroom, relevance to entity construction, reuse value, engineering cost, compute cost, validity risk
